title: Asana object identifiers, placeholders and masked Bearer values
summary: Task, project, user and workspace GIDs in a request path and a JSON body, a scheme-only Bearer header, and a Bearer value that is a placeholder, an environment reference, a template reference or a masked display.
rationale: Asana object GIDs are globally unique object identifiers, not tokens, and a bare numeric identifier must never be attributed as a credential. A scheme with no value has nothing to protect, a placeholder or reference stands in for a value kept elsewhere, and a masked display has no recoverable value.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are identifiers, placeholders, references, masked text or non-secret outputs, not credential values. That a placeholder or reference is not a value is a project decision, not a Asana statement.

sources.supports: Personal access tokens should be used similarly to OAuth access tokens when accessing the API (i.e., passing them in the `Authorization` header).

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
